title: SLO activation and domain ownership cadence
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a repeatable, lightweight sequence to move a service from intent -> live SLOs to ongoing stewardship. Focus is on getting feature teams to own measurement and first-line ops, while SRE provides tooling, escalation patterns, and governance. Aim is measurable time-to-activation and a clear handoff model so alert noise and ownership gaps shrink over successive cycles.

Scope:
- New and recently migrated services in Hosted API and Dedicated that currently lack reliable latency or error SLOs.
- Cross-functional participants: owning product/feature team, SRE reliability steward, instrumentation engineer, oncall rotation captain, and product manager.
- Excludes infra-wide platform SLOs (these are tracked in separate program).

Success criteria (what "activated" looks like):
- Two SLOs defined and committed (p50 latency and availability/error rate) with documented intent and SLI query templates in the org dashboard.
- Alerting configured to surface sustained degradation (not single spikes) with a burn-rate-style policy and annotated runbook.
- Service has assigned domain owner and weekly oncall contact in rotation schedule.
- First 30 days: no more than 1 untriaged incident related to measurement instrumentation.

Stakeholders & responsibilities:
- Feature team (owner): draft SLO intent, validate queries against prod traffic, review runbook playsteps, respond to initial triage.
- SRE (steward): provide SLI/SLO templates, verify measurement fidelity, help set alert thresholds and burn policies, run the SLO activation checklist.
- Observability eng: implement dashboards, synthetic checks if needed, optimize query cost.
- PM: prioritize timeboxed instrument/alert work in sprint.
- Support/CS: read-only access to dashboards and escalation path for customer-impacting issues.

Activation cadence (6 week lightweight sprint):
Week 0 - Kickoff (1 hour): intent alignment, identify owner, capture success criteria, link tickets.
Week 1 - Measurement baseline: SRE + observability pair to validate SLIs against 7d and 30d windows; record baseline metrics.
Week 2 - Thresholds & burn policy: propose alert thresholds, run tabletop scenarios; finalize burn-rate rules for automated suppression and priority.
Week 3 - Runbook & playbooks: create minimal triage doc (3 steps), escalation matrix, and long-lived tasks for fixes; smoke test on a canary or synthetic run.
Week 4 - Oncall readiness: add owner to rotation, simulate an incident during weekly blameless drill, confirm pager routing and escalation.
Week 5 - Stakeholder review & signoff: review dashboards, cost implications, and locked SLO definitions; PM approves schedule for production rollout.
Week 6 - Retrospective & cadence handover: measure time-to-activation, open follow-ups for reliability backlog, schedule monthly review slot.

Delivery checklist (minimum artifacts to ship):
- SLO definition doc with intent, target, and measurement window (one-pager).
- SLI queries saved in observability (templated names).
- Dashboard URL(s) and short instructions.
- Alert rules and burn-rate config with suppression windows.
- Runbook with triage steps and postmortem link template.
- Owner added to oncall schedule and contact card.

Coordination model:
- Weekly 30-minute activation sync during Weeks 0-4 with SRE steward and owner.
- Monthly reliability review after activation: review SLO trends, alert fatigue, and quality regressions.
- Quarterly program review for SLO bar adjustments and instrumentation standards.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: instrumentation creates high-cardinality cost spikes. Mitigation: impose query cost guardrails; observability eng performs preflight cost estimate.
- Risk: owner bandwidth limits progress. Mitigation: timebox activation work and allocate SRE pairing days.
- Risk: alert fatigue from noisy thresholds. Mitigation: use burn-rate and aggregated windows, ramp thresholds gradually and monitor false positive rate for first 30 days.

Open questions (to resolve at kickoff):
- Should the initial SLO window be 7/30/90 or 5/30 for this service?
- Does the service need synthetic checks or are real-traffic SLIs sufficient?
- When is the right threshold for moving to a stricter SLO in prod? (propose 90-day review).

Next steps (actions to create at kickoff):
- Create Jira ENG-XXXXX SLO activation epic and link technical tasks (measurement, dashboard, alerts, runbook).
- SRE steward to run an SLI query audit within 72 hours.
- Observability to provision a temporary dashboard and cost estimate.
- Product to block 2 days of engineering bandwidth within the next sprint for instrumentation.

Notes & references:
- Use the SLO naming convention: service.component.slo.<metric>.<window> in dashboards.
- Keep default runbook triage steps to three concise actions: verify, mitigate, escalate.
- Tag related tickets with "slo-activation" for easy discovery.

This doc is intentionally pragmatic — remove process friction and aim for short feedback loops. We'll iterate on templates after the first 10 activations to simplify further.
